source.title: SNAPSHOT USA 2024: Year 6 of the Coordinated National Camera Trap Survey of the United States

detection_calibration.protocol: reference signs every 3 m to 24 m or maximum detection distance
detection_calibration.candidate_strength: strong auxiliary detection-information path exists at aggregate level

gates.reason: new U.S. 2024 response dataset; not MICA v3, Snapshot Japan 2023, or a derivative of those empirical responses

public schemas declare the required deployment/event fields, but deployment-value parseability and identity uniqueness were not verified without opening the downloadable metadata file; 3,127 reported deployment rows versus 3,124 reported unique deployment IDs requires fail-closed follow-up

49 states, 184 arrays and four WI projects provide potential crossing, but Project×geography and calibration-array geography were not verified at deployment level without opening the downloadable metadata file
73 arrays and 918 locations have explicit calibration-distance observations, but deployment-level calibration membership must be linked response-blind before declaring a usable detection model
2715 reported physical locations greatly exceed minimum capacity, but a strict geographic train/heldout split has not yet been frozen
the frozen E5 contract requires at least six distinct calendar months in both training and heldout exposure; the complete 2024 public survey spans only August through December, five months
candidate fails G6 before any selected-candidate model contract is allowed

next_search_direction.priority: multi-season or multi-year independent camera-trap data retaining explicit detection calibration
next_search_direction.specific_option: screen SNAPSHOT USA 2024 plus a genuinely independent later season only if the combined source remains independent of E2-E4 and detection calibration can be linked without focal-response inspection
next_search_direction.do_not_do: lower the frozen six-month requirement after seeing this candidate
